title: Match Statement
prompt:
Write two functions using Python's `match`/`case` statement:

**Requirements:**
1. `http_status(code)` -- match on integer status codes: 200 returns `"OK"`, 301 returns `"Moved Permanently"`, 404 returns `"Not Found"`, 500 returns `"Internal Server Error"`, anything else returns `"Unknown"`
2. `describe_sequence(seq)` -- match on list structure: empty list returns `"empty"`, single-element `[x]` returns `"single: {x}"`, two-element `[x, y]` returns `"pair: {x}, {y}"`, anything else returns `"many: {len(seq)} items"`

files.content:
def http_status(code):
    match code:
        case 200:
            return "OK"
        case 301:
            return "Moved Permanently"
        case 404:
            return "Not Found"
        case 500:
            return "Internal Server Error"
        case _:
            return "Unknown"


def describe_sequence(seq):
    match seq:
        case []:
            return "empty"
        case [x]:
            return f"single: {x}"
        case [x, y]:
            return f"pair: {x}, {y}"
        case _:
            return f"many: {len(seq)} items"

hints: match/case is Python's structural pattern matching (3.10+)
Sequence patterns: case [x] matches a single-element list
Variables in patterns bind to matched values
